turns:
This repo has no .gitignore. Add one covering the usual Python build and cache artifacts.

Rules relevant to this task:
- Before your first write, create a branch for the task and do the work there. Never commit to the default branch. Branch names follow type/kebab-description, where type is one of feature, bugfix, hotfix, chore, release, docs.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits: type(scope): subject, where type is one of feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore, ci, build, perf, style.

events.command:
git add .gitignore && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
chore(repo): add Python gitignore

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -2 && git status --short

events.text:
Added `.gitignore` on branch `chore/add-python-gitignore`, committed as `cf105d6`.

Coverage: bytecode/`__pycache__`, C extensions, packaging and dist artifacts (`build/`, `dist/`, `*.egg-info/`, wheels), test/coverage output (`.pytest_cache/`, `.coverage`, `htmlcov/`, `.tox/`, `.nox/`), type-checker and linter caches (`.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `.pytype/`), virtualenvs and `.env`, Jupyter checkpoints, plus common editor/OS files.

Two notes:
- The repo has no packaging or venv config to infer from, so this is the standard broad set rather than something tailored — `lib/` and `var/` in particular come from the packaging convention and would need removing if you ever add real source directories by those names.
- Nothing currently tracked matches these patterns, so the commit changes no existing file state.

Not pushed — say the word if you want it on the remote or merged.
